label: Mutability of life boundaries and the receiving subject
summary:
138a151b-285a-5181-829b-5464968164ac (Bridge): 158efe69 and aa026502 use the transfer from another's power to some potency in the subject. ST I q.9 a.2 distinguishes potency in the subject from another's power over it; dependence for esse therefore needs an additional interpretation before it counts as internal changeability. Natural generation of a persistent subject is a more favorable case than creation without a prior subject. Test separately whether production or conservation gives a real passive potency inhering in that same bearer, keeping a merely extrinsic dependence separate.

473f3a7f-0730-5bdc-a7e2-772c8372ffd7 (Variant): aa026502 preserves the specific MUTABLE_2 life-boundary reading, while c6356524 certifies that it implies the weaker MUTABLE_3 sibling. The latter suffices in 158efe69 with the same 138a151b transfer. This reduction provides no warrant that every boundary is a case of another's power. Retain the stronger branch for the explicit scope comparison.
blocker: Power in another must be connected to a passive potency of the same subject in an admitted respect.
